$comment: GENERATED by scripts/units/year/type-work-list.js. Never edit by hand.

A.title: Read a little book with a pattern
A.differs: 7 English picture readers (I See Pets, At the Farm, My Lunch ...): cover + three pages of one patterned sentence each; K-630 is the same book to colour, K-631 the Read and Talk companion page.

A.title: Vowels and consonants
A.differs: K-230 sorts letters into vowels and consonants; K-533 colours every vowel in picture words (L1 four 3-5-letter words), the second half of the objective.

A.title: Read a decodable book
A.differs: 5 English decodable mini-books (Dad and Sam, Kit and the Dog ...), every word gated to the taught sounds and heart words, no pictures: the child reads each page and draws it; K-631 is the companion page.

A.title: The pictures and the words
A.differs: Level 1 (one story of four sentences): the child numbers the sentences and draws a line from each to its picture. The 'stories' are four-step picture sequences (an apple eaten bite by bite, a fence being painted), not a tale with characters; the teacher reads the sentences.

A.title: In, on, under, next to
A.differs: Maths-catalogue type (K.G.A.1, Position Words maker). K-548 level 1: in, on top of, under, next to; level 3 adds behind and in front of (circle the word that fits the sentence for each scene). The relation is a picture and a shape, not a cat and a box. K-546 (published) is the need's level 3: read the sentence and draw the picture in place.

A.title: Blends at the start: st, fl, tr
A.differs: Initial blends (bl br cl cr dr fl fr gl gr pl pr sk sl sm sn sp st sw tr tw; 57 pictures): L1 circle the blend of three, L2 write the two letters before the printed rest (__og), L3 from the picture. A page spreads over all blends (no s-blends-only level 1), about a third of the words have two or more syllables (bracelet, broccoli, dragonfly), and there is no read-and-match half. G1-333 adds blend word-family ladders.

A.title: Find the answer in the story
A.differs: Level 1: a 43-73-word story with numbered sentences and 3 literal questions (who, what, where, when, why), each with a 'Sentence N' chip that sends the child to the sentence holding the answer. 3 multiple-choice questions, not 4; the stories are not strictly decodable (pumpkins, librarian); the child is shown the sentence rather than underlining it. G1-504 asks the same passages as open questions on lines (3/4/5 questions).

A.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
A.title: Long or short vowel?
A.differs: Level 1 (six one-syllable words): the child says each word and circles the long line or the short dot. The word is printed with its vowel coloured (the spelling shows the length) and all vowels mix; there is no cut-and-sort into two boxes and no one-vowel level.

A.title: Two texts on one topic
A.differs: The ready material of the grade-2 point (en-2-078) serves here too: two printed animal fact files (class, habitat, diet, covering), circle same or different for each fact, then write two things that are the same and two that are different. The 'texts' are fact-file tables, not 40-word running texts, and there is no fact-strip sort level.

A.title: Compound words and two-part words
A.differs: G2-330 Split the Compound (draw a line where the second word starts; L1 shows the parts) = level 1; G1-324 Syllable Cards (read the word one syllable at a time, L1 two syllables) = level 2 (rabbit, picnic); G2-332 Compound Detective (12 words, circle the 6 compounds and write their parts) = level 3. Three pages, not one; no picture of each small word.

A.title: Short or long vowel?
A.differs: Level 2 (eight one-syllable words) or level 3 (two-syllable words too): say the word, circle the long line or the short dot; long = silent e or ai ay ee oa igh ie. Marking, not sorting into two columns; no hop/hope sentence choice.

A.title: Two animals: same and different
A.source: reuse:Compare Two Animals: Same and Different

A.title: Root words as clues
A.differs: G3-399 Root Words in Sentences writes four family words above a root stone into sentence gaps (meaning from the shared root); G2-359 sorts derived words onto their roots; G2-375 finds the shared root. Eight English families (help, play, care, use, joy, fear, act, sleep); the child shows the meaning by using the word, not by writing a definition.

A.title: Past tense: regular and irregular verbs
A.differs: Level 2/3: a table of six pictured verbs (today form and past) + sentence gaps; the 28-verb bank has regular (jumped, hopped, carried, giggled) and irregular pasts (ran, slept, threw, caught, built, hid). G2-337 chooses the form in a sentence, G2-334 matches verbs to past forms. No regular/irregular mark column, no present-tense story to rewrite.

use.title: Front cover, back cover, and title page
use.differs: K-629 / K-628 are real fold-up mini-books (one sheet folded twice): a front cover with the title (K-628 adds an illustrator line) and three pages with one sentence each. They have no title page, no back cover, no page numbers and no tasks (circle the title, star the back cover, number the pages, match cover/title/page). Far: a print-concepts mode of types/_shared/reader-book.js with an 8-page fold, title page, back cover and the three task levels.
use.note: built: Front Cover, Title Page, and Back Cover (the three parts of a drawn book to circle, to label by cut and glue, and the page where the story starts); with K-666 Make a Front Cover and a Title Page

use.title: Read left to right, top to bottom
use.differs: The mini-books practise tracking in a real book: K-629 'point under each word as you read', page by page; K-628 pages break over 2-3 lines ("Kit the cat | sat on a mat."), so the return sweep happens. No page prints start/stop dots or left-to-right and return-sweep arrows to trace or draw, and none asks to number the words. New layout (print-concepts page), not a small change.
use.note: built: Read Left to Right, Top to Bottom (a green dot where reading starts, a red dot where it stops, an arrow under each line and back to the next line); with K-668 Number the Lines and the Pages

use.title: One spoken word, one written word
use.differs: K-552 Sentence Strips prints 2-4 picture sentences as one word card per word that the child cuts apart and rebuilds (one card = one word), and K-629 has the child point under each word; neither has the row of empty boxes to colour one per spoken word, nor the 3-word / 4-5-word sentence ladder. Small change: a box row under each K-552 sentence.
use.note: built: One Spoken Word, One Written Word (the word among a letter, a digit and a scribble; one dot under each word of a sentence the teacher says); with K-670 Match the Word You Hear

use.title: Spaces between words: count the words
use.differs: K-552 makes the word boundaries physical (cut the sentence into word cards); K-527 Trace a Sentence has the child copy a sentence (finger spaces). Nothing asks to draw a line in each space, count the words and write the number. Small change: a count-the-words mode over the K-552/K-527 sentence bank.
use.note: built: Spaces Between Words, Count the Words (a line in each space, the number of words); with K-672 Finger Spaces (the sentence that is easy to read, word cards to cut and glue with spaces)

use.title: Short a and short i
use.differs: K-227 Middle Sounds: CVC pictures, the child writes the middle vowel; K-224: write the missing (vowel) letter. Both mix all five vowels on every page and cannot be limited to short a / short i; the K-227 bank holds 18 words (a 6, i 3, o 4, u 3, e 2), too few for twelve words of one vowel. No read-the-word-and-match half, no two-column sort. G1-306 has -an and -at families (onset writing). Small-to-moderate change: a vowel unit axis + a larger CVC bank.
use.note: built: Short a and Short i: words to read and match to pictures, the vowel to write, words to sort under a or i, the word to write for a picture

use.title: Short o, short u, and short e
use.differs: Same as en-K-008: the medial-vowel pages mix all vowels and the bank is thin (o 4, u 3, e 2 words in K-227); no one-vowel page, no read-and-match half, no two-column sort. Needs a vowel unit axis and a larger CVC bank.
use.note: built: Short o, Short u, and Short e: words to read and match to pictures, the vowel to write, words to sort by vowel, the word to write for a picture

use.title: Change one sound to make a new word
use.differs: No word-chain / word-ladder page exists. Build a 'chain' mode of types/_shared/lit-word-build.js (the K-224/K-231 factory): a bank of CVC chains where each step changes one letter (first, last, then middle), with pictures.
use.note: built: Change One Sound to Make a New Word, a ladder of six words; the teacher says each change, the child writes the new word (first sound; first or last; first, middle or last)

use.title: Which word matches: cat or cot?
use.differs: G1-330 Word Families: Read and Circle shows a picture and a column of words from the same rime row (can / fan / pan / van) and the child circles the one that names it: real words differing in the FIRST letter only (the need's level 1). Nothing pairs words differing in the last letter or the middle vowel (cat/cot, pin/pen), and nothing asks to underline the letter that differs. G1-552 compares a word with misspellings (non-words). Small change: a minimal-pair bank with first/last/middle levels.
use.note: built: Which Word Matches? One Letter Is Different: two words that differ in the first, the last or the middle letter beside a picture; the word to circle and the letter to underline

use.title: Who is in the story, and where?
use.differs: G1-506 Story Map is the organiser (L1 boxes Beginning 'Who is in the story? Where are they?', Middle 'What happens?', End, each with a draw box and 2 lines) for any read-aloud, but it prints no story and has no picture choices. G2-254's stories (30-73 words, narratives) ask who/where among 3 word-choice questions, not pictures. Moderate: a read-aloud picture-panel story bank + Who/Where/What-happened boxes.
use.note: built: Who Is in the Story, and Where?, a read-aloud story in four picture panels; who, where and what happens to circle, to draw, to draw and name with a word

use.title: Retell the story: beginning, middle, end
use.differs: K-381 is the need's level 1 (cut out three pictures, glue them in First / Next / Last; L1 one strip), G1-401 the level-2 drawing (draw the middle between the given beginning and end). But the strips are wordless object-change sequences (an apple eaten, a fence painted), not a story with characters read aloud, and there is no retell frame (First ___. Then ___.). Moderate: a read-aloud story bank on the same layouts.
use.note: built: Retell the Story: Beginning, Middle, End, three pictures of the story to number, three boxes to draw in, three big rows for First, Then, At the end

use.title: Ask and answer questions about a story
use.differs: G2-254 has stories the teacher can read (L2 published pool 44-73 words) with 3 key-detail questions (who, what, where, why, how does X feel) but the answers are three printed WORDS/phrases, which a kindergartner cannot read; no picture answers and no own-question box. Moderate: picture-answer questions for a short read-aloud story.
use.note: built: Ask and Answer Questions About a Story, who and where questions, what and how questions with pictures to circle, and a box for a question of the child

use.title: Naming words and action words
use.differs: G1-293 Nouns and Verbs: Two Bins, level 1: 3 nouns + 3 verbs, the nouns with a small picture, the child copies each word into the naming or the doing bin. The verbs have no picture (a kindergartner cannot read them), the child writes rather than cuts and pastes, and there is no 'The ___ can ___.' frame. Small change: action pictures (library 'activities' theme) and a cut-and-sort mode.
use.note: built: Naming Words and Action Words, cards to cut and glue into two boxes; with K-658 Find the Action Word

use.title: A sentence starts with a capital letter
use.differs: G1-498 prints sentences in small letters only and the child circles every word that needs a capital: the first word, the word I and names (L1 four sentences, L3 rewrite). Sentences are 5-8 words (not 3), names are mixed in, and no page prints mostly correct sentences with a few small-letter starts to fix. Small change: a K level with 3-4-word sentences and no names.
use.note: built: A Sentence Starts with a Capital Letter, three- and four-word sentences without names; with K-660 Fix the First Letter

use.title: A period or a question mark?
use.differs: G2-282 level 1: broken sentences (no capital, no end mark, one name) that the child rewrites with a capital and the right end mark, . or ?. It asks a K child to rewrite whole sentences, has no pictures and no half-telling/half-asking structure for writing only the mark. Small change: a 'write only the end mark' K level with pictures.
use.note: built: A Period or a Question Mark?, circle the mark, write the mark, write a sentence; with K-659 Telling or Asking? Sort the Sentences

use.title: Say more: make the sentence longer
use.differs: G1-503 Stretch the Sentence: a short sentence (The big dog plays.), the questions Where? When? (How? from L2) with a line each, then the longer sentence. Same skill (expand with where/when/how) but no picture, no box of add-ons to circle or copy; the child must invent and write the phrases (G1 demand). Small change: a K level with a picture and a printed add-on box.
use.note: built: Say More: Make the Sentence Longer, a picture, a short sentence and three add-ons to choose from and to write

use.title: Ask and answer questions about a fact text
use.differs: There is no information-text-with-questions page. The nearest is G2-343 Who Am I? Mystery Animal: three cards of five first-person fact clues and a bank of six animal pictures (answer = the animal: a picture choice). It answers 'who am I', not who/what/where/how questions about a 30-word fact text, and is G2 reading. Far: an information-text bank (30-80 words per grade) with picture-answer questions.
use.note: built: Find the Facts, a fact text of four sentences in big print; four questions answered by circling one of three pictures, by drawing, or by drawing and asking a question of their own

use.title: What is it all about? The main topic
use.differs: G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two passages without titles, circle the title that fits of three: the main-topic idea. The passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts, the answers are printed titles (no pictures), and there are no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: What Is It All About?, the same texts; circle the picture of the whole text, then circle or draw its key details

use.title: Pictures that teach
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G2-364 Parts of a Plant and Their Functions: five job phrases (root 'takes in water from the soil', stem, leaf, flower, seed) matched to numbered tags on a plant picture by writing the tag number: the text-to-picture link the lesson teaches. One level only (five parts), phrases not a four-sentence text, numbered tags instead of word labels; G1-376 labels the parts from a word bank (the level-3 'add a label'). Small change: a 2-/4-label K ladder and a line-drawing answer.
use.note: built: Pictures That Teach, a line from each sentence of a fact text to the picture that goes with it (three sentences, four, four with one picture to draw); the labeled plant picture of the design gave way to the pictures of each text

use.title: First this, then that: connect two ideas
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G1-203 The Life Cycle of a Chicken: number three pictures 1-2-3 (egg to chick, the need's own example); G1-377 the butterfly. There is no information text to read and no 'First ___, then ___' frame; it sequences pictures rather than connecting two ideas in a text. Small change for the picture part; the text needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: First, Then, a fact text that tells a change, a question that names it, and two boxes joined by an arrow (cut and glue, draw, draw and write a word)

use.title: Two texts, one topic
use.differs: G2-342 Compare Two Animals: two printed animal fact files (class, habitat, diet, covering), circle same or different per fact, then write two same and two different: a G2 reading/writing load with no running text and no picture cards. G3-393 (science) checks butterfly / frog / both per sentence. Far: two read-aloud texts on one topic + a picture-card Venn sort.
use.note: built: Two Texts, One Topic, two fact texts of four sentences on one topic and six pictures to sort into first text only, both texts, second text only (cut and glue, draw, draw and name)

use.title: ck, ng, and wh
use.differs: Of the three spellings only ck exists: the G2-315 rule 'c, k or ck' (G2-324 Which One?, G2-326 sort) has ck words (sock, lock, duck, rocket) mixed with c/k choices. No ng and no wh unit in any type (G1-311 Sound of the Week has sh, ch, th only). Small change: ng and wh units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js or the letter-of-the-week bank.
use.note: built: Digraphs: ck, ng, and wh, words to build from old words, to match with pictures, to sort and to finish in sentences

use.title: Blends at the end: nd, mp, st
use.differs: No final-blend bank exists. G1-306 has one final-blend family, -and (hand, sand), among CVC rimes; G1-493 does INITIAL blends only. Small change: a final-blend bank (nd, mp, st, nk) for the G1-493 factory.
use.note: built: Blends at the End, nd, mp, st and nk: words to build, to match, to sort and to write under pictures

use.title: Characters, setting, and big events
use.differs: G1-506 is a story map but its boxes are beginning / middle / end (L3 + problem), not characters / setting / big events, and it prints no story; G2-254 prints stories (43-73 words) whose questions touch who and where but carry no story map. Small change: a characters-setting-events box set in G1-506 + a story from the G2-254 pools.
use.note: built: Characters, Setting, and Events, a story of about 70 words; the two characters among four animals, the setting and the big event to circle, to write in a few words, to write as a sentence

use.title: Retell the story and tell its lesson
use.differs: Retelling exists: G2-378 Retell with Starters (one 4-picture sequence, write each picture starting First / Next / Then / Finally; L1 one line each) and the G1-506 story map. No fable bank and no lesson / central-message line anywhere (G2-488 picks a title, not a lesson). Far: a fable bank with lesson choices.
use.note: built: Retell the Story and Tell Its Lesson, three sentences to order, a word bank, the retelling in the own words; the lesson beside the lesson of another story

use.title: Words that show feelings
use.differs: K-319 Feelings matches six faces to feeling words (part of level 1); G2-254 asks 'How does X feel?' about its stories. No page has the child underline feeling and sense words in a story or poem, and no sense words appear. Moderate: a short story/poem bank with tagged feeling and sense words.
use.note: built: Feeling Words and Sense Words, two feeling words with their faces and two sense words with the part of the body, in a story that holds no other feeling word

use.title: Who is telling the story?
use.differs: No page asks who is speaking (narrator or character). Build a dialogue-story bank with speaker tags; the speech-bubble frames of G1-507 (writing-frames.js bubble) could carry level 1.
use.note: built: Who Is Telling the Story?, six sentences of a story with three spoken lines: the narrator or one of the two characters

use.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
use.title: Silent e changes the vowel
use.differs: G2-315 unit 'Magic e' (a_e i_e o_e u_e; 48 picture words, L1 3-8 letters): read the rule box, write the vowel and the final e into the gaps. Mostly long words (lemonade, telephone, porcupine), no cap/cape pairs, no 'add an e and read the new word' task, no a_e-only level. Small change: CVC/CVCe pair bank + a vowel-by-vowel level.
use.note: built: Silent e Changes the Vowel, pairs to finish (cap, cap_), pictures with the two words of a pair, sentences one word of a pair fits; a_e, then a_e and i_e, then all four vowels

use.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
use.title: ai and ay
use.differs: The G2-315 rule 'ai or ay' exists (fill the gap; G2-326 sorts picture words into an ai bin and an ay bin; G2-324 circles ai or ay) but its 21 words hold only 2 ay words (playground, haystack), too few for the sort faces, most are two-syllable (raincoat, sailboat, waitress), and 6 are not long a at all (chair, armchair, hair, stairs, eclair, wheelchair: /air/). Small change: a corrected long-a bank with one-syllable ai and ay words.
use.note: built: Long a: ai and ay, one-syllable words to match, finish, sort and write, with the rule of the place in the word

use.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
use.title: ee and ea
use.differs: The G2-315 rule 'ee or ea' exists (40 words; G2-326 sort into ee / ea bins) but mixes words where the letters do not spell long e: ear, earmuffs, deer, reindeer, meerkat (r-controlled) and cereal, theater (e and a in two syllables); most words are two-syllable. Small change: clean the bank to one-syllable long-e words.
use.note: built: Long e: ee and ea, one-syllable long-e words to match, finish with a picture, sort and write

use.unit: Long Vowels: Silent e and Vowel Teams
use.title: oa and ow
use.differs: The spelling-rules factory has no oa/ow unit (en units: magic-e, c-k-ck, ee-ea, ai-ay, floss, y-ies-f-ves). Small change: an oa-ow rule unit in data/b3/spelling-rules.js; the pages (gap, sort, which one) exist.
use.note: built: Long o: oa and ow, one-syllable words to match, finish, sort and write, with the rule of the place in the word

use.title: Names, days, and months get capitals
use.differs: G1-498 Capital Letters: sentences in small letters, circle each word needing a capital (first word, names, I; L3 rewrite). Its 18 sentences hold names only; the generator states that weekdays and months are not in them. No date or own-name writing. Small change: sentences with days and months.
use.note: built: Names, Days, and Months Get Capitals (words to circle and write again, the date, the own name, the birthday month); with G1-593 Capital Letter or Small Letter? (the word to choose in a sentence)

use.title: Joining words: and, but, so, because
use.differs: No conjunction page exists. Build a join-two-sentences mode over the tagged sentence bank (data/grammar/grammar-tables.js, types/_shared/sentence-items.js, the G1-502 Sentence Halves factory) with an and/but/so/because box.
use.note: built: Joining Words and, but, so, because: the word that fits best to circle in sentences with pictures, two sentences to join in writing (the key gives a sample and the other right forms)

use.title: Yesterday, today, tomorrow: verb tense
use.differs: G2-317 Verb Forms (en 'today and yesterday'): a table of six pictured verbs with the columns 'he/she today' and 'yesterday' + three sentence gaps; the bank mixes 14 regular (jumped, hopped, carried) and 14 irregular verbs. No 'tomorrow / will' column and no regular-only level. Small change: a future column + a regular -ed level.
use.note: built: Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow: a table of regular verbs with one form missing in each row, then one verb written three ways

use.title: Write a true story: plan and draft
use.differs: G1-506 Story Map plans a story (beginning / middle / end boxes with prompts, draw box + 2-3 lines); G2-378 writes a picture sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally starters. No true-story planner with first/next/last + a 6-line draft page, no time-word frames on every line, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Plan a True Story (a short true story to mark: the time words, the events in order; a plan in three boxes to draw with a row for notes); with G1-617 Write a True Story (the draft with First, Next, Last and an ending)

use.title: My opinion and a reason
use.differs: No opinion-writing page exists. Build an opinion frame (opinion box, reason box, I think ___. One reason is ___. That is why ___., checklist) with the starter/line/box pieces of types/_shared/writing-frames.js (G1-506 / G1-509 family).
use.note: built: Opinion or Reason? (sentences sorted as opinion or reason; each opinion matched to its reason; because to circle); with G1-619 Write My Opinion (a question to choose, a drawing, the opinion on a frame with because and an ending)

use.title: All about a topic: facts and a closing
use.differs: G2-341 Fact File: Write Three Sentences: a printed animal fact file, finish three sentences with its facts, then one fact of the child's own. The topic is always a given animal, there is no topic sentence frame, no closing sentence and no checklist; G2-318 is the empty fact file to research. Small change: an informative frame (This is all about ___ ... Now you know ___).
use.note: built: Facts and a Closing (a fact file with a picture; sentences that are about the topic or not; the closing sentence to choose); with G1-621 Write an All About Page (a topic, three facts, a closing, a drawing with two labels)

use.title: Revise and edit with a checklist
use.differs: G2-274 Fix the Sentence covers the edit half: broken sentences (no capital, no end mark, lowercase names) rewritten on lines, with a checklist banner (A · Aa · .?!). There is no sample piece with mixed mistakes, no revise check (add a detail, heart words), and no checklist for the child's own draft. Small change: a checklist page in writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Edit and Add a Detail (a piece by a first grader with a small letter at the start, a missing end mark and a small i to fix; the star sentence written again with a detail); with G1-623 Revise with a Checklist (a partner question, the detail added, a Me and Partner checklist)

use.title: A duck is a bird that swims: words by category
use.differs: Category sorts exist (K-240 cut, sort and paste into 2-3 bins; K-511 sort by a rule; K-550 name the group), but on broad categories (animals, fruits, vehicles, clothes), not birds / fish / bugs, and nothing asks for a definition 'A ___ is a ___ that ___'. Small change: sub-category bins + a definition-frame row.
use.note: built: Words by Category, Cut and Sort (picture cards to cut and glue under birds, fish, insects, fruits, vegetables, toys or tools; on Level 3 two cards fit no box); with G1-609 A Duck Is a Bird That Swims: Define Words

use.title: Endings -s, -ed, and -ing
use.differs: G2-317 writes a verb's -s form ('he/she today') and its past (regular -ed and irregular mixed) in a table; G2-337 circles the fitting form of three under a sentence. No -ing column anywhere, irregular pasts mix in, and no 'circle the base word'. Small change: an -s/-ed/-ing column set with regular verbs only.
use.note: built: Add -s, -ed, and -ing (the base word to circle, a table of the three forms; doubling and dropping e on Level 3); with G1-611 Which Ending Fits? (the form a sentence needs, to circle and to write)

use.title: Ask and answer: facts in the text
use.differs: G1-504 Read and Answer has the right shape (a passage, 3/4/5 key-detail questions with answer lines) but its passages are narrative stories (30-73 words), not information texts with a heading and a picture; G2-343 reads animal fact clues. Moderate: an information-text bank (about 70 words) for the G1-504/G2-254 pages; the question formats exist.
use.note: built: Read the Facts, an informational text of about 60 words with two headed parts; four questions to circle, to finish from a starter, or to write and underline in the text

use.title: The main topic and key details
use.differs: G2-488 Which Title Fits?: two untitled passages, circle the title of three (main topic). Narrative stories, not information texts; no key-detail boxes. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Main Topic and Key Details on the same texts (circle the topic and copy a detail; write the topic and two or three key details)

use.title: Text features: headings, bold words, a glossary
use.differs: No text-features page exists (no text with headings, bold words, captions or a glossary anywhere in the banks). Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.
use.note: built (nothing was close): Use the Text Features, find-it questions from headings, bold words, caption and glossary, with G1-578 Name the Text Features as the page before it

use.title: Every syllable has a vowel
use.differs: G1-329 Vowel King is exactly this (every syllable has one vowel: dot the vowel in each printed syllable arc) but it is REFUSED for English by design (bank kings:false; published in de and sv only). G1-305 counts syllables by clapping and drawing arcs, not by vowels. Small change: enable English with a closed-syllable word filter (napkin, basket).
use.note: built: Every Syllable Has a Vowel (vowels to underline, the number of syllables to write, words to match with pictures); with G1-601 One Syllable or Two? (a sort and the two-syllable word to circle in a sentence)

use.title: Tricky words: said, was, of, could
use.differs: Sight-word pages exist (K-437 missing letters, K-433 read-trace-write + sentences, K-390 one sentence step by step); said and was are in the English word list, of, could and would are not. No sound boxes with a heart over the tricky part. Small change: add the words + a heart-word mapping mode in types/_shared/sight-word-pages.js.
use.note: built: Heart Words said, was, of, could: sound boxes, a heart over each tricky part, sentences written from memory behind a fold

use.title: Vowel teams for long a, e, and o
use.differs: Two of the three pairs exist as G2-315 rule units (ai or ay, ee or ea; G2-326 sorts into two bins) but oa/ow does not, the ai-ay bank has only 2 ay words and 6 /air/ words (chair, hair, stairs ...), and the ee-ea bank holds r-controlled and split-vowel words (ear, deer, reindeer, cereal, theater). No all-six-teams page. Small change: an oa-ow unit + cleaned long-a / long-e banks.
use.note: built: Vowel Teams for Long a, e, and o (ai, ay, ee, ea, oa, ow): the team to choose, words to sort and to write in sentences

use.title: oo, ou, ow, oi, and oy
use.differs: The spelling-rules factory (gap, sort, which-one pages) has no oo, ou/ow or oi/oy unit in English. Small change: three rule units in data/b3/spelling-rules.js (with the oi-middle / oy-end and ou-middle / ow-end rule).
use.note: built: Vowel Sounds oo, ou, ow, oi, and oy (words to sort by sound, ou or ow and oi or oy to choose); with G2-543 Reading Words with oo, ou, ow, oi, and oy (yes or no, riddles, read and draw)

use.title: How characters meet a challenge
use.differs: G2-254 level 3: 2 inference questions + 1 written answer about stories with a small problem (a tower washed away, a stuck ball) and 'How does X feel?' questions. Stories are 58-73 words (not ~150), there is no challenge / what-the-character-did / feeling organizer and no quote-as-proof. Moderate: longer stories + an organizer layout.
use.note: built: How a Character Meets a Challenge, a fable of about 135 words in beginning, middle and end; the problem, what the character does, a feeling; with G2-527 What Happens and Why (causes and effects)

use.title: Fables: what is the lesson?
use.differs: Retelling exists (G2-378: write a 4-picture sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally), the moral does not: no fable or folktale in any bank and no lesson line (G2-488 chooses a title). Far: a fable bank (~150 words) with retell strips and lesson choices.
use.note: built: What Is the Lesson?, the lesson among the lesson of another fable and a literal sentence, two events that show it; with G2-529 Beginning, Middle, and End (three sentences to order, the retelling written)

use.title: Plan and draft a true story
use.differs: G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end, draw box + 2 lines each) plans a story; G2-378 drafts a picture sequence with time-word starters. No who-and-where / feelings planner for a personal small moment, no 10-line draft page, no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Parts of a True Story (a true story by a second grader: the time words to circle, the feeling or thought to underline, the events to number, the ending to choose or to write); with G2-572 Plan Your True Story (who, where and when, what happened in order, how I felt) and G2-573 Draft Your True Story (beginning, middle and ending from the plan)

use.title: Revise and edit a story with a checklist
use.differs: Only the editing part exists: G2-282 / G2-274 rewrite broken single sentences (capital, names, end mark) with a checklist banner. No sample story with mixed mistakes, no revise checks (detail, stronger word, word-wall spelling), no checklist for the own draft.
use.note: built: Edit a Story (a story by a second grader with counted mistakes: capitals and end marks to fix, sentences to number in order, on the hardest level a sentence that does not belong; two sentences written again); with G2-575 Revise with a Partner (a Me and Partner checklist, the partner question, the detail added with a caret, a sentence fixed)

use.title: ar and or
use.differs: No ar/or unit in the spelling-rules factory (English units: magic-e, c-k-ck, ee-ea, ai-ay, floss, y-ies-f-ves). Small change: an ar-or rule unit; the gap, sort and which-one pages exist.
use.note: built: Bossy r, ar and or (words to sort, to finish and to write); with G2-544 Reading Words with ar and or

use.title: er, ir, and ur: one sound, three spellings
use.differs: No er/ir/ur unit in the spelling-rules factory. Small change: an er-ir-ur rule unit (three bins on the G2-326 sort face).
use.note: built: er, ir, and ur, One Sound, Three Spellings (the spelling that looks right, words to sort in three columns); with G2-545 Reading Words with er, ir, and ur

use.title: Long vowels in two-syllable words
use.differs: Two-syllable reading pages exist (G1-325 write the word with a dash at each break, G1-331 join two syllables, G1-324 read the word in parts) but none marks the long vowel or groups words by kind (vowel-team compound / silent e / open first syllable), and the English splits follow dictionary hyphenation (bak-er, bik-ing, hik-ing, skat-ing), which contradicts the open-syllable rule of level 3 (pa-per, mu-sic). Moderate: a decoding-split bank by syllable type.
use.note: built: Long Vowels in Two-Syllable Words (words to split, the long syllable to circle; vowel teams, silent e, open syllables by level); with G2-547 Build and Read Two-Syllable Words

use.title: Tricky words: could, would, should
use.differs: The sight-word pages exist but none of could, would, should, because, friend is in the English word list (Dolch pre-primer to grade 1), and there is no sound-box + heart mapping. Small change: add the words + a heart-word mode.
use.note: built: Heart Words could, would, should (sound boxes, a heart over the tricky part, sentences written from memory behind a fold); because, friend, people and others on levels 2 and 3

use.title: The main topic of a text and of each paragraph
use.differs: G2-488 picks the title that fits a whole passage (main topic) but its passages are one-paragraph narrative stories (30-73 words); no three-paragraph information text, no per-paragraph focus. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Main Topic and Paragraphs, an informational text of about 150 words as three numbered paragraphs without title or headings; circle the main topic and give each statement its paragraph, or write topic and focus, or also a heading

use.title: Text features: captions, bold words, glossary, index
use.differs: No text with captions, bold words, subheadings, a glossary or an index exists. Build an information-text bank with marked features and a find-it question page.
use.note: built (nothing was close): Glossary and Index, the same texts as a small book page with headings, bold words, two captioned pictures, a glossary and an index; six find-it questions to circle or to write, and on the hardest level an index entry and a glossary entry to add

use.title: What the diagram shows
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G2-365 Label the Butterfly Life Cycle: write the four stage names from a bank under their pictures and cross out the name that does not belong; G1-377 numbers the stages. No 120-word text and no questions answered from the diagram or from text + diagram. Moderate: a short text + diagram questions on the G2-365 layout.
use.note: built (the science page was not close enough): What the Diagram Shows, a text of two paragraphs and a cycle diagram of drawn stages with labels and arrows; questions from the diagram, what the diagram adds, a label and an arrow to add; with G2-524 Text or Diagram? as its second page

use.title: Steps in order: how it is made
use.differs: G2-378 Retell with Starters writes a 4-step process sequence (making a sandwich, painting a fence, building a snowman) with First / Next / Then / Finally; G1-402 orders the sentences of a sequence. Pictures, not a 150-word how-it-is-made information text, and no 'why must this step come first'. Moderate: process texts on the same layouts.
use.note: built: Steps in Order, a how-it-is-made text of four steps (First, Next, Then, Finally) with three pictures; number the steps, write them in a flow chart, tell why one step comes before another; with G2-525 Before and After as its second page

use.title: Plan an informative piece
use.differs: G2-318 Animal Fact File groups facts by fields (class, habitat, diet, covering, + legs, fly) on one animal with a draw box; G2-381 My Habitat Report. The topic is given (an animal / a habitat), there is no introduction line, no free fact groups and no checklist. Small change: an informative planner in writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Parts of an Informative Piece (the topic sentence, the definition and the closing sentence to mark in a short piece; facts to sort under two headings, an opinion and a sentence about something else to cross out); with G2-566 Plan Your Informative Piece (a topic sentence, three facts, a definition and a closing sentence planned from a box of facts)

use.title: Draft with facts and a closing
use.differs: G2-341 turns a printed fact file into three sentences + one own fact. No 12-line draft under group headings, no linking words in the margin, no definition, no closing, no checklist.
use.note: built: Closing Sentences and Linking Words (the closing sentence to choose among a new fact, an opinion and the topic sentence again; a definition to write; also, another or and to circle); with G2-568 Draft Your Informative Piece (the piece written from the plan, with frames, starters or open lines and a checklist)

use.title: Research with two books: a class report
use.differs: G2-318 is the note-taking fact file for a class research topic (W.2.7), but it gives no source texts; G2-342 prints two fact files. No two 80-word texts, no question-led organizer, no report page with heading. Far: two-text research set.
use.note: built: Research with Two Books: Take Notes (two short books of 40 to 60 words each on one animal or job, a table of what each book tells, notes in a few words with the book they came from); with G2-570 Write Your Part of the Class Report (a heading, three sentences from the notes, a labeled picture, cut out for the class report)

use.title: Prefixes un- and re-
use.differs: Split over two pages: G2-376 reads the meaning and writes the prefix for re- / pre- / mis- (10 rows; only reread, refill, retell for re-), G2-320 adds un- / dis- / in- to make the opposite (L1 prints the prefix). No un- + re- page with 'not ___ / ___ again' meaning matches and no sentence gaps. Small change: an un-/re- prefix-key set in data/b5/word-parts.js.
use.note: built: Prefixes un- and re-: the new word to write for a meaning, words to match with meanings, un or re to write in a sentence

use.title: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly
use.differs: G2-359 sorts derived words onto their root's wall: families help, play, care, use, joy, fear, act, sleep with members such as helpful, helpless, careless, playful, sleepily. The suffixes appear but the child sorts by ROOT and never says what -ful / -less / -ly adds; no meaning match, no build-the-word sentences. Small change: a suffix-meaning mode over the same bank.
use.note: built: Suffixes -ful, -less, and -ly: the base word to circle and the suffix to underline, words to match with meanings, the suffix to write in a sentence

use.title: Apostrophes: can't and the dog's bone
use.differs: No contraction or apostrophe-possessive page exists. The owner-and-thing picture layout of G2-354 (Possessive Pronouns, G1-352 factory) could take a possessive-noun mode; contractions need a new word-pair page.
use.note: built: Apostrophes: contractions to write and to expand, the owner with an apostrophe and s, the word of a sentence that needs its apostrophe

use.title: Spicy, juicy, crunchy: words in real life
use.differs: No page links describing words to real things. Build a describing-word bank with draw-or-name boxes; nearest pieces: the adjective bank of G1-509 (data/b3/opposites.js) and the G1-396 shades-of-meaning rows.
use.note: built: Describing Words in Real Life (the picture or the two things a word describes, six words to match with pictures, the word a sentence needs); with G2-550 Draw and Write with Describing Words

use.title: Adjective or adverb?
use.differs: No page has adverbs (the word-class banks hold nouns, verbs, adjectives). Build an adjective/adverb pair bank on the G2-337 choose-the-form layout (two forms under a sentence) with an arrow-to-the-word task.
use.note: built: Adjective or Adverb? (the form that fits to circle, an arrow to the word it tells about; a sort, two frames to fill, sentences of the own by level)

use.title: Plan an opinion: reasons and linking words
use.differs: No opinion planner exists. Build it in types/_shared/writing-frames.js (opinion box, three reason boxes, closing box, linking words, checklist).
use.note: built: Parts of an Opinion Piece (the mixed-up sentences of a piece sorted into opinion, reasons and closing sentence; because, also, and in gaps); with G2-558 Plan Your Opinion Piece

use.title: Draft an opinion piece
use.differs: No opinion draft page exists. Build it in writing-frames.js (12 lines under opinion / reasons / closing headings, linking words in the margin, checklist).
use.note: built: Write Your Opinion Piece (the draft under Opinion, Reasons and Closing sentence); with G2-560 Revise Your Opinion Piece (the reason or the closing sentence a piece needs, a partner check, a sentence to add)

use.title: A friendly letter
use.differs: G1-510 Write a Postcard, level 3 = a letter on the whole page (8 lines) with 'Dear ___,' and 'Love,' printed. No date line, no labelled parts, the commas are printed (not practised), no sample letter with missing commas, no second reader. Small change: a letter-parts level.
use.note: built: Parts of a Friendly Letter (the five parts named on a letter; the commas after the greeting and the closing); with G2-562 Write a Friendly Letter (a reader and a topic to choose, a letter frame)

use.title: Capitals for holidays, places, and brand names
use.differs: G1-498 is the circle-the-capitals page, but its sentences carry only names, I and the first word; no holidays, places or product names, and no needs-a-capital sort. Small change: a sentence set tagged for holidays / places / brands.
use.note: built: Special Names: Find the Capital Letters (the words missing their capital to circle; names sorted as holiday, place or product name); with G2-564 Special Names: Write the Capital Letters (sentences written again with their capitals)

use.title: Closed and open syllables
use.differs: Syllable pages exist (G1-325 write the word with a dash at each break, G1-326 missing syllable) but none names closed or open syllables, and the English splits are dictionary hyphenation (bak-er, bik-ing) and, in the broader pool, closed-first splits for open-syllable words (tig-er, rob-ot, pap-er), so they cannot teach ro-bot / ti-ger. Far: a decoding-split bank by syllable type + a C/O marking mode.
use.note: built: Closed and Open Syllables (a line between the syllables, C or O in a box for each, the word that fits a sentence); with G3-513 Closed or Open? Sort Long Words

use.title: Silent-e, vowel-team, and consonant-le syllables
use.differs: No page names syllable types; consonant-le words (table, puzzle) are not in the English syllable pool at all. Far: a syllable-type bank (silent-e, vowel-team, C-le) and a name-the-type mode on the G1-305 factory.
use.note: built: Silent-e, Vowel-Team, and Consonant-le Syllables (split each word and type each syllable, then sort); with G3-515 Build Long Words from Syllables

use.title: Suffixes -able, -ment, -ness, -ful, -less
use.differs: The word-part families carry the suffixes (helpful, helpless, carelessness, enjoyment, enjoyable, fearlessness) but the child sorts by root (G2-359) or fills sentence gaps (G3-399); no circle base / underline suffix / meaning match, no -ness/-ment-focused level, no base-changes level (happiness). Small change: a suffix mode over data/b5/word-parts.js.
use.note: built: Base Words and Suffixes (-able, -ment, -ness, -ful, -less: the base to circle, meanings to match, words to build in sentences); with G3-517 Which Word Fits?

use.title: Tricky words: enough, though, ocean
use.differs: The sight-word pages exist but the English list is Dolch pre-primer to grade 1: none of enough, though, ocean, laugh, through. Small change: grade-3 heart words + a heart-word mode.
use.note: built: Heart Words enough, though, ocean (sound boxes, a heart, sentences written from memory behind a fold); with G3-519 The Sounds of ough

use.title: Show where the story says it
use.differs: G2-254 level 1 numbers the sentences and points each literal question to its sentence (evidence), level 3 adds a written answer. Stories are one paragraph of 58-73 words (need ~250 words in numbered paragraphs), 3 questions, no box for the proving paragraph, no copying the exact words. Moderate: longer grade-3 stories in the same Level Set format.
use.note: built: Show Where the Story Says It, a fable or folktale of about 210 words in four numbered paragraphs; the answer, the paragraph, the proving sentence; with G3-503 Ask and Answer About a Story

use.title: Fables and folktales: the central message
use.differs: G1-506 L3 is a recount organizer (beginning / problem / middle / end); there is no fable or folktale bank and no message line or detail lines (G2-488 picks a title). Far: a ~250-word folktale bank with message choices.
use.note: built: The Central Message, the message among the message of another story and a literal sentence, three events that show it; with G3-505 Retell the Story

use.title: Characters: traits, feelings, and actions
use.differs: Some G2-254 pool questions ask about traits and feelings ('What kind of brother is Yusuf?', 'How does Zara feel?'); G1-509 describes a pictured character with adjectives. No 250-word story with a changing character, no character web with proof lines, no cause-and-effect chain. Moderate.
use.note: built: Character Traits, a trait with the sentence that shows it and a feeling at the end; with G3-507 Cause and Effect in a Story

use.title: Context clues
use.differs: No context-clue page exists (the cloze pages G1-350 / G2-350 fill a gap with a pictured word). Build a ~200-word passage bank with bold unknown words and marked definition / example / opposite clues.
use.note: built: Context Clues, What Kind of Clue? (one sentence with a new word; the clue to underline, its kind D, S, A or E, the meaning to circle or to write); with G3-541 Context Clues in a Passage

use.title: Use a dictionary and a glossary
use.differs: Only the ABC-order part exists: G1-264 orders words that share a first letter by the second letter. No dictionary page, no guide words, no choosing among meanings, no spelling check. Far.
use.note: built: Use a Dictionary, Guide Words and Meanings (a dictionary page of twelve entries: the page a word is on, the meaning a sentence uses, the right spelling, an entry to write); with G3-543 Use a Glossary: Find the Meaning

use.title: State an opinion and plan the reasons
use.differs: No opinion planner exists. Build it in types/_shared/writing-frames.js (introduction, opinion, three reasons with a fact line each, conclusion, checklist).
use.note: built: Opinions and Reasons (fact or opinion for six sentences; the opinion, the reasons and the conclusion of a short piece to mark; one more reason to write); with G3-549 Plan Your Opinion Piece

use.title: Reasons with linking words
use.differs: No opinion draft page exists. Build it in writing-frames.js (16 lines under the planner headings, linking words in the margin, checklist).
use.note: built: Choose the Linking Word (because, since, therefore, for example in a blank; two sentences to join); with G3-551 Draft Your Opinion Piece

use.title: End with a concluding statement
use.differs: No page works on conclusions. Build a short-opinion-piece bank with weak endings + conclusion choices, on writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Find the Conclusion (the concluding statement among a new reason and a change of subject); with G3-553 Write a Conclusion

use.title: Revise and edit an opinion piece
use.differs: Only sentence-level editing exists (rewrite broken sentences: capitals, names, end marks). No sample opinion paragraph, no revise checks (support, linking words, commas), no peer box. Far.
use.note: built: Edit an Opinion Paragraph (capitals, end marks, a comma, a missing linking word, a sentence that does not belong); with G3-555 Revise Your Opinion Piece (a checklist for the child and a partner, a comment, a sentence to add)

use.title: What each word does in a sentence
use.differs: G1-497 circles one word class in short sentences (L1 nouns, L2 verbs, L3 adjectives); G2-287 sorts 15 words into noun / verb / adjective bins. No pronouns or adverbs, no labelling of every word, no five-column sort. Small change: P and Adv tags in data/grammar/grammar-tables.js SENTENCES + a label-all mode.
use.note: built: Sort the Parts of Speech (words written under noun, pronoun, verb, adjective, adverb; two words of the own for each job); with G3-530 Label the Parts of Speech (N, P, V, Adj, Adv under every word of a sentence)

use.title: Plural nouns: regular and irregular
use.differs: G2-349 Plural Nouns writes the plural into a sentence under cloned pictures; level 3 forces at least three harder plurals (foxes, buses, cherries, strawberries, wolves, geese); G2-328 drills y→ies and f→ves. Irregular plurals: only goose→geese (no mice, teeth, children), no rule column. Small change: irregular frames in data/b4/cloze-levelset.json + a rule column.
use.note: built: Which Plural Is Right? (the right plural among the singular and common misspellings, in a sentence); with G3-532 Plural Nouns: Spelling Rules (the plural to write with the number of its rule; irregular plurals on Level 3)

use.title: Subjects and verbs agree
use.differs: G2-485 Conjugation Table makes the verb agree with I / you / he / she / we / they (play, plays); G2-337 chooses the form that fits a sentence. Noun subjects (The dog runs / The dogs run), words between subject and verb and pronoun-antecedent agreement are missing. Moderate: an agreement sentence bank.
use.note: built: Subjects and Verbs Agree (the verb that agrees to circle, an arrow to its subject; two subjects, There is and There are, pronouns on Level 3); with G3-537 Fix the Words That Do Not Agree

use.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
use.title: Answer with evidence from an information text
use.differs: The question shape exists (G2-254 L1 points each question to its numbered sentence; G1-504 open answers) but all passages are narrative stories of 30-73 words: no 250-word information text with headings, photo and numbered paragraphs, no paragraph-number box. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Answer with Evidence, an informational text of about 230 words in four numbered paragraphs with headings; the answer, the paragraph that proves it, on the hardest level the proving sentence; with G3-495 Ask and Answer (which question a sentence answers, questions of their own)

use.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
use.title: Main idea and key details
use.differs: G2-488 picks the title that fits a short story (main idea of a narrative). No four-paragraph information text, no main-idea + three-details organizer, no summary. Needs an information-text bank.
use.note: built: Main Idea and Key Details, the same texts without their headings; the main idea among one too narrow and one too broad, three key details, a summary; with G3-497 The Main Idea of Each Paragraph

use.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
use.title: Text features and search tools
use.differs: No text with a table of contents, sidebar, key words or index exists. Build an information-text bank with marked features and find-it questions.
use.note: built: Use the Text Features, the text as a small book (table of contents, key words in bold, sidebar, glossary, index); with G3-499 Which Text Feature?

use.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
use.title: Maps, diagrams, and photos
use.differs: Science-catalogue types. G3-385 The Water Cycle: Label the Diagram (write four words from a bank on the numbered diagram, the need's topic); G1-379 reads a map key. No 200-word text, no rain map, no questions that combine text and picture. Moderate.
use.note: built: Read the Text and the Map (five texts with a grid map of real places) and G3-511 Read the Text and Diagram (five texts with a chain of steps); every question is marked map or diagram, text, or both

use.unit: Information Texts: Main Idea and Text Features
use.title: Time order and cause and effect
use.differs: Time-order sequencing exists only with pictures (G2-378 writes a 4-step sequence with First / Next / Then / Finally; G1-402 orders sentences). No 250-word historical or science text, no timeline, no cause-and-effect chain. Far.
use.note: built: Events in Order, four events or steps on a chain First, Next, Then, Finally with a because-sentence; with G3-501 Cause and Effect (match, the missing half, one sentence with because or so)

use.title: Take notes and sort them
use.differs: G2-318 Animal Fact File is a category note-taking organizer for one animal (class, habitat, diet, covering, legs, fly, swim) but gives no source texts and no source line; the need's categories are body / food / home. Far: two 150-word source texts + a 3-box note organizer.
use.note: built: Choose and Sort Notes (the best note for a sentence; notes sorted under headings; one that fits none); with G3-557 Take Notes and Sort Them (notes in own words from one and from two sources)

use.title: Introduce a topic and group the facts
use.differs: The fact file (G2-318) and My Habitat Report (G2-381) group facts about a given topic with a picture, but there is no introduction box, no heading lines, no caption and no checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Introductions and Groups (the sentence that introduces all the notes; a heading for each group); with G3-559 Plan Informative Writing (a planner with an introduction, three headings and a concluding sentence)

use.title: Facts, definitions, and details
use.differs: G2-341 writes three fact sentences + one own fact from a printed fact file. No 16-line draft under headings, no definition frame, no linking words, no concluding section, no checklist.
use.note: built: Fact, Definition, or Detail? (the job of each sentence of a paragraph; a definition and a detail for a fact); with G3-561 Develop Your Topic (the draft in three parts with a definition, linking words and a concluding sentence)

use.title: A short research report
use.differs: The research-record pages exist for one animal / one habitat, but there is no question box, no two given source texts, no report frame with headings and diagram box, no source list. Far.
use.note: built: Notes from Two Sources (a research question, Source A and Source B, a note chart by category); with G3-563 Write a Research Report (introduction, three parts, a diagram with a caption, a concluding sentence, the sources)

use.title: Joining words: and, but, so, because, when
use.differs: No conjunction page exists. Build a join-two-sentences mode on the tagged sentence bank (types/_shared/sentence-items.js, G1-502 factory) with coordinating and subordinating conjunctions.
use.note: built: Choose the Joining Word (the word and its comma written in the blank; and, but, or, so, because, when, if, after, before by level); with G3-520 Join Sentences with Joining Words

use.title: Simple, compound, and complex sentences
use.differs: No sentence-type page exists. Build a simple / compound / complex sort on the tick-or-cross classification of G1-501 (sentence-items.js) plus a combine-the-sentences rewrite.
use.note: built: Simple, Compound, and Complex Sentences (the kind of each sentence to check); with G3-523 Build Compound and Complex Sentences (two short sentences written both ways)

use.title: Better, best: comparing with adjectives and adverbs
use.differs: G2-484 Comparison of Adjectives: six adjectives, write the comparative and superlative (L1 comparative only, L3 up to two irregulars good/bad). Its 15 adjectives are all -er/-est or irregular: no more/most, no adverbs, no sentences to complete. Small change: more/most rows + adverbs in data/grammar/grammar-tables.js COMPARISON.
use.note: built: Comparing Words, Choose the Right Form (-er or -est, more or most, the irregular forms, by the sentence); with G3-524 Better, Best: three animals to compare and a table of forms

use.title: Possessives: the dog's bone, the dogs' bones
use.differs: No apostrophe-possessive page exists (G2-354 does possessive PRONOUNS). Build a possessive-noun mode on the G2-354 owner-and-thing layout plus a plural-or-possessive choice.
use.note: built: Possessive Nouns, One Owner or More (the possessive to write and to choose); with G3-527 Add the Apostrophe: Fix the Possessives

use.title: Capitals in titles
use.differs: G1-498 is the circle-the-words-needing-a-capital page (L3 rewrite) but for sentence capitals and names; no titles and no rule that a, the, of, in stay small. Small change: a title bank with a title-case rule.
use.note: built: Find the Capitals in Titles (the words of a title that need a capital to circle); with G3-528 Capitals in Titles (titles to write with their capitals)

use.title: Plan a story: characters, setting, problem
use.differs: Level 3: Beginning (Who is in the story? Where are they?), Problem (What goes wrong?), Middle (What happens?), End (How does it end?), each with a drawing box and 2 lines. One middle box (not three events), no story-mountain picture, no checklist.
use.note: built: The Parts of a Story (the characters, the setting, the problem and the narrator of a story beginning); with G3-565 Plan Your Story (a story mountain and a planner); the older story map G1-506 is not used

use.title: Dialogue and description
use.differs: G1-507 Comic Strip: 3-4 frames with an empty speech bubble per speaker (L3 a caption line). The child writes speech in bubbles but never turns it into sentences with quotation marks and commas, and nothing adds actions or thoughts. Moderate: a 'bubble to quoted sentence' level.
use.note: built: Quotation Marks in Dialogue (the sentence written the right way for a speech bubble; lines to punctuate); with G3-567 Show Feelings in a Story (showing instead of telling, dialogue with said-words)

use.title: Time words that order the events
use.differs: G2-378 writes a picture sequence with the starters First / Next / Then / Finally (grade-1 time words). No 16-line draft under event headings, no grade-3 time phrases (later that day, after a while), no ending box, no checklist.
use.note: built: Time Words in a Story (events to number by their time words; the time word that fits a tiny story); with G3-569 Write with Time Words (the draft under Beginning, Middle and Ending)

use.title: Revise for words that work
use.differs: G2-374 replaces said with a stronger word that fits each sentence; G3-397 sorts words for go and look into word fields. No sample paragraph with eight underlined weak words (went, said, looked, nice) and no 'mark three words in your draft'. Small change: a revise-the-paragraph page over the same banks.
use.note: built: Choose a More Exact Word (the one word that fits the sentence; the clearer sentence and why); with G3-571 Revise for Words That Work (a paragraph with tired words, sentences of the own)

use.unit: Point of View and Comparing Texts
use.title: Chapters, scenes, and stanzas
use.differs: No play, poem or chapter text exists in any bank. Build a short play (two scenes) and poem (three stanzas) bank with part-naming questions.
use.note: built: Scenes and Stanzas (a play with scenes and a poem with stanzas: where something happens, how a part builds on the one before, a next scene to write); with G3-573 Chapters: How Parts Build

use.unit: Point of View and Comparing Texts
use.title: Whose point of view?
use.differs: No first-person opinionated story and no point-of-view chart exists. Build a story bank with a narrator's view + a two-column chart on writing-frames.js.
use.note: built: Who Is Telling the Story? (a character who says I or a narrator outside the story; what the teller thinks); with G3-575 Their View and My View (a view chart, a part retold as another character)

use.unit: Point of View and Comparing Texts
use.title: Literal and nonliteral language
use.differs: No literal / nonliteral (idiom) page exists. Build an idiom bank with meaning choices (the circle-the-meaning card of G2-358 Synonyms could carry it).
use.note: built: Literal or Nonliteral? (a phrase that means just what it says or a saying with another meaning; the meaning to write); with the screen activity of the point

use.unit: Point of View and Comparing Texts
use.title: Two books by one author
use.differs: No page compares two stories by one author. Build a paired-story bank on the two-card compare layout of G2-342 (rows setting / problem / plot / theme).
use.note: built: Two Stories by One Author (sentences sorted as Story 1, Story 2, both or neither); with G3-578 Compare Two Stories (a chart of lesson, setting, problem and ending)

use.unit: Point of View and Comparing Texts
use.title: Two texts on one topic
use.differs: Science-catalogue G3-393 Butterfly and Frog Life Cycles Compared checks butterfly / frog / both for each sentence (a sentence Venn); G2-342 compares two animal fact files. No two 200-word information texts on one topic, no two-circle diagram to fill, no comparing sentences. Moderate.
use.note: built: Two Texts on One Topic (two information texts side by side; facts sorted into a two-part diagram: only Text 1, only Text 2, both); with G3-580 Compare Two Texts (the most important point and the key details of each text, how the texts are alike and different)

G1-314.title: Blend the first sound and the rest
G1-314.differs: G1-314 Blend the Sounds prints the word's sounds in boxes (L1 3-4 sounds) and the child blends them and circles the matching picture of three. It is phoneme-by-phoneme blending from PRINTED letters, not oral onset-rime blending the teacher says (/s/ ... /un/), and it has no levels by distractor kind (different first sound / same first sound / same rime). Moderate change: an oral 'teacher says it' mode with no letters and rime-controlled picture triples.
G1-314.note: change: an oral 'teacher says it' mode with no letters and rime-controlled picture triples

K-554.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
K-554.title: My favorite and why: an opinion
K-554.differs: K-554 My Reading Log names the book (title, author), rates it with stars, asks 'My favorite part' and a drawing; K-342 has the child circle a favourite picture and copy its word. Neither has the opinion frames 'My favorite ___ is ___. I like it because ___.', a word bank or the 3-icon checklist. Small change: an opinion frame with the writing-frames.js starter blanks.
K-554.note: an opinion frame with the writing-frames.js starter blanks

G1-509.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
G1-509.title: Teach a fact: draw, label, and write
G1-509.differs: G1-509 Describe the Character: a big picture and the starters My character's name is ___ / is ___ and ___ / likes ___ / lives in ___ with a word bank (L1-2): describing a pictured animal, not the child's own topic, and no labelled drawing box. K-555 gives a picture and one line; G2-318 a fact file of one animal. None prints This is a ___. It has ___. It can ___., a box for a labelled drawing or the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506.unit: Draw and Write: Opinions, Facts, and Stories
G1-506.title: What happened to me: a small moment
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map L1: beginning / middle / end boxes with a draw box and 2 lines each, prompts about a story (Who is in the story?), not a personal small moment. Missing the two picture boxes First/Then, the frames First I ___. Then I ___. I felt ___., the word bank and the checklist. Small change in writing-frames.js.

G1-506.title: How a story begins and ends
G1-506.differs: G1-506 Story Map L3 (beginning / problem / middle / end) is the arc organizer; G1-401 draws the middle between a beginning and an end. Neither prints a story (~150 words) or asks what the beginning introduces and how the end solves the problem. Moderate: a story bank with the arc questions.
G1-506.note: a story bank with the arc questions

K-326.title: First, middle, or last sound?
K-326.differs: K-326 Beginning, Middle or End: the child colours the box where the week's letter sound is heard; level 1 = beginning or end only (3-0-3), level 3 = four middle cards: the need's ladder. But the pictures are words of any length (mailbox) and 'middle' is a consonant inside a long word, not the vowel of a CVC/CCVC word; K-227 covers the medial vowel separately. Small change: a one-syllable picture filter and vowel units.
K-326.note: a one-syllable picture filter and vowel units

D.title: Two stories, two adventures
D.differs: No page compares two stories. Build a paired-story bank (two short read-aloud stories with panels) on the two-card compare layout of G2-342 (compare mode of G2-318) or a Venn cut-and-paste like K-240.

D.title: Words with two meanings
D.differs: No multiple-meaning (homograph) page exists. Build a two-picture homograph bank (bat, duck, ring, bark, top, can) as a mode of the word-picture matcher types/_shared/lit-vocab-match.js (K-225).

D.title: Different voices for different characters
D.differs: No dialogue story and no speaker/point-of-view task exists. Build a dialogue-story bank with speaker tags; the G1-507 speech-bubble frame could carry the 'what would each say next' part.

D.title: Two versions of one tale
D.differs: No page compares two versions of a tale. Build a paired-tale bank on the two-card compare layout of G2-342 (rows characters / setting / problem / ending).
